notes.title: Alchemic Beast Interactions
notes.content:
Hey everyone!

Welcome to another dev log for Alchemic Beasts! Lately, I've been working on a system that personifies(?) the beasts that you capture. All of the beasts have a personality and come with some traits that make them who they are. They can interact with other beasts and with you! Any time a social event happens it will be displayed in the beast's life log as well as in the menu as their latest social event.

When they interact with other beasts in your party, they may form a bond making it more likely that they breed into something with much better stats and give a better outcome for variants and transmutations if they are compatible for that type of thing. Otherwise they just become friends or enemies.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/6f503e58400c563ca83e2f6087310974c062a3a4.png[/img]
(Not actual player options, also don't mind all the test stuff! This is my testing room)

These interactions don't happen on the map, as cool as that would be, but they happen in text. The system is in its very early stages, but it is mostly working. Whenever a beast interaction happens, you can choose to acknowledge it which interrupts gameplay or ignore it and continue playing because it ain't your business.

If you acknowledge it, you'll be given some options to affect the beasts even further, like if their feelings got hurt, you can comfort them, or if they were being a jerk, you can discourage them from doing that behavior.

Depending on the beast's personality, you might further upset them or they can have a specific reaction to your meddling. This will be displayed as icons next to the option (current placeholder is a green eyed crazy face). You can only choose one reaction of the bunch, so you'd want to choose carefully.

This is a system I've been dying to put into the game since we started. It gives it such a digimon/tamagotchi feel and I feel like it helps you become attached to the beasts to see their whole journey from capture/birth to death in their life log.

Say the kringle in this scenario pictured above is your best beast. He's been loyal the whole time, has some strong moves and great stats, and he's welcoming to all the other beasts that may join the team. Then this happens and you have jerkface Hookwinger laughing at his misfortune.

Would you high five Hookwinger and commend that behavior or would you join Hookwingal, and offer him encouragement. Tell him he'll get it next time? The choice is yours... And the choice will affect his growth in some way, shape, or form!

It has been so fun making this system and seeing the beasts interact with each other... well not actually SEEING it, but picturing it in my mind.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/5e9dc539f9065d855e72dd19e423af404c4bc295.png[/img]

You get some really funny interactions sometimes, but it can also be because the system is being janky, haha. Those are the things that I need to iron out.

We hope you like it so far!

If you’d like to support us as we continue to forge our world, the [url=https://celestialtear.com/]Celestial Tear[/url], check out our [url=https://www.patreon.com/c/CelestialTear]Patreon[/url]! Stay tuned for more!


- Yin & Rell

notes.title: Alchemic Beasts: Breeding And Transmutation
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/62aa0bf74f77ff0b5ef64c3822e50bdf5439c0d6.gif[/img]

Hi everyone!

We have been hard at work on Alchemic Beasts, trying to get a tech demo complete so that we can either run a kickstarter campaign or pitch to publishers. I've been working on the beast breeding and transmutation system. The tech demo will feature most, if not all, of the main mechanics and features that we want to have in the game and will take place in a small story-less tech demo room or area.

The video above shows two hookwings breeding to become a Blazwing. There are so many things that factor into the evolution or variation of a beast. Let me explain it!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/8128482f0ff1e653c3f9ee3d7944d1db6cff526c.png[/img]
Each one of these beasts has a full tree of possibilities! At the bottom, we have the base beast and it's variants. When breeding, beasts can "evolve" horizontally. These are called variants and are possibly naturally occurring through breeding or cross-breeding beasts of the same type and life stage. They are mostly palette swaps, but we wanted them to still be cool, so we gave them some elemental pizzazz!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/3aaf186a22bada2d9527ea22fd2a5f61c8c29bf9.png[/img]
To get to a new tier, you would have to transmute the beasts with a medium. With alchemy, you'll see some pretty crazy things. In this particular tree, we have the heatheren and its variants as the next tier of creatures.

A heatheren, the one in the middle, is the natural air evolution to a hookwing.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/2b1896a90165ddc3c4e7a865e6c1bbc502cb0e23.png[/img]
On the next tier, things get really wild. We have true dual elemental transmutations. Going from left to right, we have a firzome (fire and air), harkwin (water and air), zabeak (pure air), coreaper (nature and air), and goblem (void and air). These can only be achieved through alchemy, so at this point we're no longer breeding in the normal sense. There has to be mediums involved in the creation of these beasts.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/18c1e96d6df43d2271fc630e0b9db8d30adbd0f6.png[/img]
Beyond that, we have a metasaur and quarvar. These are considered "ultimates" and usually have all types of different metals mixed into their designs. These ultimates are mixes of 3 elements and are usually very powerful and hard to obtain.
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/047af9e40da01257b9c64167473b41bd0c0ac010.png[/img]
You will notice that for the Zabeak, I used the term "pure air." This is because it can only be acquired by having a purebred hookwing chain. A purebred hookwing chain is a hookwing ancestry that has never deviated from being air. There can be no variations or non-air transmutations in its ancestry. It would have to be 2 air hookwings to make the heatherens, 2 air heatherens to make the zabeak. I think this will be more for hardcore players who want to... "transmute 'em all", for lack of a better phrase. This beast can be considered an ultimate although it is not technically in the top tier (visually on the chart).

All beasts have a similar structure when it comes to breeding an transmutation except for the shellodon. Keep in mind that it is a celestial beast, so of course it would be special in some way! We'll get into that in a future update!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/c0c5130a4f0c90d2dd9cf4c1bbee535695812860.gif[/img]
This is the menu that you will be doing your beast alchemy in! It's not finalized yet, but it's pretty packed with information. Where it says no requirements, if there is something special that you need to do to get a certain outcome, there will be a list of requirements that need to be met and they will be green or red depending on if the requirement has been met.

Though you can't choose directly what the beasts will breed into, you can definitely help them along to the one that you want by meeting as many of the requirements as you can. The lines change between green and red with green being definitely possible, yellow/orange being maybe, and red being NOPE, these are impossible odds. Once you breed or transmute a particular beast, it will no longer be blacked out.

What do you think about breeding and transmutation so far? Who would you main from this tree? Do you have any questions about the process of breeding or evolving? We'd love to hear your thoughts so make sure you comment!

Thank you for reading!

If you’d like to support us as we continue to forge our world, the [url=https://celestialtear.com/]Celestial Tear[/url], check out our [url=https://www.patreon.com/c/CelestialTear]Patreon[/url]! Stay tuned for more!

Don’t know what Alchemic Beasts is? Look no further than here:

notes.title: Variants!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/46ef08dce409e49e17a27164dbcdffdee8db7269.png[/img]

Hey Everyone!

In Alchemic Beasts, we have a plan to create over 200+ unique beast graphics between 5 different species and 6 elements. In there, we have outliers who can't evolve or have very short evolution chains. We've now been talking about the possibility of variants.

Unlike the other creatures, visually, these variants would be palette/body part swaps of already existing creatures.For example, we have an Ostalcoatl in the image above, on the left. It's water variant would be an Aqualotl which is on the right side. They'd have front and back views for battle, menu graphics and everything that a normal beast would have. These variants don't change the creatures into something new like alchemic breeding and evolution does. Technically it changes their graphic and gives them some resistance among other possible stat changes. Based on if a body part has changed, a new move is also possible, but a new move is not guaranteed.

For extra reference, here are what the baliskin variants look like!
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/211995f679927434fc5151e376873dce2881305e.png[/img]
From left to right, we have: Nagliskin, Zyteskin, Baliskin, Valcorin, and Soacarin!

We just thought it was a cool idea and it adds a bit more to the alchemy part of Alchemic Beasts. Which one is your fav so far? I'm definitely into the Soacarin's sleek design!Thank you all for you support! Let us know what you think :D

- YIn & Rell, White Guardian Studios

notes.title: Alchemic Beasts Starters
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/bae64f9dccf706461496d7623e5d2d3dc2e3c232.png[/img]

Hey everyone!

We are so excited to be included in the Creature Collector Fest! During the week, we will be dropping some dev logs about the game.

Today we want to talk about the starting beasts in Alchemic Beasts! You've seen them all on the key art and maybe even through some of the videos that we put out, but now we're going to officially talk about them!

In Alchemic Beasts, we have a system of beasts that are based on elements and types:

Elements - [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/d8bab4e1906aefeb66a23e9d55def0f535bd6b29.png[/img]

*Void and celestial elemental beasts are rare, the latter being super rare.

Types - [img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/76a3bc4b096f04a03b8bdf0bd4c227304dcdf98f.png[/img]
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/a6d6d9d93096369133f5652fd5385f6de8fa2a2a.png[/img]
Baliskin

Baliskins are lizards that have adapted to feed off sunlight, often found basking on tropical beaches where they absorb large amounts of energy. Their spines, green from photosynthesis, store around 10,320 volts of electrical energy (about the amount stored in an electric fence), with each spine holding approximately 860 volts. This surplus of energy enables baliskins to perform remarkable defensive feats: they can launch their spines in self-defense or discharge a powerful 9,460-volt plasma burst, which leaves them temporarily exhausted. These abilities make baliskins nearly self-sufficient, and their intimidating appearance serves to ward off potential predators.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/518e6dd4ee10107d73f26bcda12080f5bf46bf4c.png[/img]
Hookwing

Hookwings embody the phrase “biting off more than you can chew.” These remarkable creatures dive at incredible speeds, using their hard, bowl-shaped beaks to scoop up fish. Their signature "hooked wings" defy physics, rotating in a circular motion like a hummingbird's to hover momentarily before making sharp dives into the water. However, a hookwing’s real secret lies in the unique design of its wings and beak. If pulled underwater, it can store air in its beak and release it in a jet-like stream, propelling itself through the water at speeds up to 20 miles per hour. Afterward, it returns to its usual routine, swiftly scooping fish from the water’s surface.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/cfc437295351be4141c38c0081fda57fe85d5419.png[/img]
Orchid

The orchid is an energetic, forest-dwelling creature known for its fiery hunting methods and obsessive grooming habits. Its floating mane generates enough friction to ignite small fires, which it uses to flush out insects hiding in tree bark. Despite their potential for destruction, these fires rarely threaten the forest, as other creatures—such as water-bearing reptiles and moisture-manipulating plants—quickly step in to douse the flames. This balance has made the orchid's fire-starting a natural part of the ecosystem.

Orchids are also highly vain, spending significant amounts of time grooming their manes, which are essential for both attracting mates and survival. In territorial disputes, male orchids target each other's manes rather than using fire, as a damaged mane signals vulnerability. A well-groomed mane is a symbol of strength, while losing one leaves the orchid unable to hunt or defend itself, marking its downfall in the wild.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/c47398c42adb36da048354b00d7649c63a319164.png[/img]Megsquito

Megsquitos are a unique breed of mosquito that appeared seemingly out of nowhere and swiftly out-competed their relatives, becoming an invasive species in many swamp ecosystems. Their rapid spread has led to significant ecological shifts, forcing entire ecosystems to adapt. The only predator capable of preying on them is the murkin, though even murkins become intoxicated from the megsquito’s potent toxins and are left stumbling around in daylight.

Megsquitos possess the unusual ability to phase in and out of dimensions, enabling them to summon reinforcements when threatened. Their venom is unnaturally potent, capable of inducing hours-long nightmares in their victims, and their proboscis harbors multidimensional bacteria. Fortunately, megsquitos have a vulnerability: at room temperature and below, their venom solidifies, causing them to fall from the air and perish.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/f4719cd1f3775ecf3d573557d31ac6d2b953d5ae.png[/img]
Buzzel

On the surface, buzzels appear to be harmless little fish, and for most sea creatures, they are. But when land animals wander too close to shore, they must be wary of these brightly colored beasts of the sea. When a buzzel senses surface ripples, they enter a frenzy, striking at the source of the disturbance. Usually traveling in packs of five, they leap from the water with powerful force, dragging their prey beneath the waves. Each pack has its own unique choreography, but the goal remains the same: pull the target underwater, drown it, and devour it.

[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/a66fe3a8d8347830586da32ec21e88632056a3d1.png[/img]
Shellodon

Shellodons are a peaceful species, preferring to conceal themselves within their impenetrable stone shells, which provide natural, formidable protection. These amphibians drag their shells onto land to keep their bodies moist while they search for their favorite plants. First sighted near ocean-side craters, shellodons gradually spread out over vast distances, becoming so rare that encountering one is uncommon. When discovered, they are easily lured out by the scent of their favorite food, the gigandus. The gigandus is a sparse fern that grows only around Mizu. When trained, shellodons make ideal bodyguards due to their unwavering loyalty and long lifespans, often living for decades.

Whew! This was quite a long one! Thank you for reading! Let us know what you think! 

What starter would you choose? I've personally have been starting with the megsquito. I don't know, something about its colors and the whole void thing it has going on has me intrigued!

Thank you all for your support! Stay tuned for more!

- Yin & Rell, White Guardian Studios

notes.title: Alchemic Beasts Update: Unleash Unique Abilities!
notes.content:
[img]{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/45016001/86dda4076bdadd8890dc7d11272a59fe9aee87f9.gif[/img]

Hey everyone!

We’re excited to dive into the special abilities that make each beast in Alchemic Beasts stand out! 🧪

Every monster in the game has its own distinct set of abilities tied to its elemental core, body type, and evolution stage. Whether it's a fiery creature that unleashes scorching flame bursts or a stone giant with powerful earth-shaking stomps, no two beasts fight the same way.

Here's a peek at what you can expect:

Elemental Mastery: Some beasts harness their elemental core for devastating attacks. Fire-based beasts can scorch opponents, while water-based creatures have the power to freeze or heal.

Adaptive Evolution: As your beasts evolve through alchemy, their abilities shift and grow, letting you tailor their strengths and tactics to fit your playstyle.

Strategic Body Parts: Beasts with razor-sharp claws might specialize in high-speed critical hits, while those with tough shells rely on defense and counterattacks. Some may even have long-range abilities like poisonous stingers or electric shocks!

With over 200 unique monsters to capture and evolve, the possibilities for creating your ultimate team are endless. Which beast will you master?

Stay tuned for more updates as we continue to build and refine the Alchemic Beasts experience!

Thank you for your support, and we can't wait to see how you evolve your beasts!
